note: Re-judged 2026-11-19 after 50b89fb51b (reserved band removed) and 6cf8d9289d (equal orders refused). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy." The tag set changed: TestSpdOrderCannotCaptureTheIKEControlPlane and TestSPDPolicyOrderInsideBypassBandRefused are gone with the IKE bypass band, and TestSPDPolicyEqualOrderOnOverlapRefused is the new negative. Positive TestSpdOperatorOrdersOverlappingPeers is unchanged: two peers with overlapping 0.0.0.0/0 selectors at policy-priority 500 and 1500 install both directions at exactly those ranks and in that order. Negative TestSpdUnstatedOrderTakesTheDefaultRank changed only its failure text: an unstated order never reaches the SPD as 0 and takes PriorityChildSA. Negative TestSPDPolicyEqualOrderOnOverlapRefused drives verifySPDOrder (called from config verify, engine/config.go): overlapping operator entries at one order, and an operator entry at an overlapping peer's policy-priority, are refused with an operator error naming both entries, the shared order and the exact set ... order fix; overlapping entries at distinct orders, disjoint entries at one order, and an entry beside a peer bound to an XFRM interface (another SPD) are accepted. That is the case just outside the clause: a configuration whose order the administrator left undecided is refused, while every decided order is accepted. The operator entry's order reaching the kernel is proven elsewhere (TestRFC4301OrderedInboundSearchRefusesOnTheFirstRankedDiscard reads back rank 1000) and is not claimed here. Verdict stands.
